lines.text: Sorting is everywhere — search results, leaderboards, your music by artist. It starts with one small move: the swap.
To swap two cups of juice you need a third, empty cup.
Code is the same: copy one value into temp first, or it gets overwritten.
Compare each pair of neighbours from left to right.
If they’re in the wrong order, swap them.
After one pass, the biggest value has “bubbled” to the end.
Put the three swap blocks in a My Block with an input i.
It swaps item i and item i + 1.
Now the pass is easy to read.
A list of n items has n − 1 neighbouring pairs, so one pass makes n − 1 comparisons.
Python can swap in one line — but underneath, it still needs somewhere to keep a value while it moves the other.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
